question: Are inexpensive observation-only action baselines already competitive, and can a pooled motion probe transfer across episodes?
status: frozen before probe execution; the primary neural interface experiment is unchanged
models: ridge from joints plus current point mean/std and past validity fractions
same ridge plus past displacement mean/std at each of15 lags
selection: leave-one-training-episode-out CV on16 training episodes; minimize pooled valid-scalar full-chunk action MSE; validation never selects alpha
normalization: training-fold mean/std only, std floor0.001; centered targets, unpenalized intercept; objective mean squared residual plus alpha times coefficient squared norm
motion_control: Both geometry and motion probes receive identical past-valid fractions; only the motion probe receives pooled current-relative past displacements. Same present points and no future features.
interpretation: A positive transfer is evidence for this restricted probe's predictive utility, not closed-loop benefit or a necessary information upper bound. A negative pooled linear probe cannot rule out useful nonlinear or spatially resolved motion information. Four reused validation episodes are development evidence only.
